chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: Null and Undefined are both data types in JavaScript.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: Undefined is a variable that has been declared, but not assigned a value.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: Null is an assignment value, so you can assign the value null to any variable, which basically

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: means it's blank.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: So by not declaring a value on a variable, JavaScript automatically assigns the value

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: to Undefined.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: But JavaScript will never automatically assign the value to null.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: That must be done specifically by you in your code.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: Let's get some more info on these.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: We see here that the type of null is an object.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: The type of Undefined is Undefined.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: Since these are different data types, if we compare them with strict equality, triple

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: equals, we get false.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: But if we compare them with abstract equality, double equals, we get true.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: So JavaScript does consider these to be relatively equal, since they are both basically blank.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: So if you need to check to see if a value is either null or undefined, you can check

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: for abstract equality by using the double equals sign and compare it to either null

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: or undefined.

chunks.title: JavaScript Null vs Undefined
chunks.text: Both will return the same result.

text: Null and Undefined are both data types in JavaScript. Undefined is a variable that has been declared, but not assigned a value. Null is an assignment value, so you can assign the value null to any variable, which basically means it's blank. So by not declaring a value on a variable, JavaScript automatically assigns the value to Undefined. But JavaScript will never automatically assign the value to null. That must be done specifically by you in your code. Let's get some more info on these. We see here that the type of null is an object. The type of Undefined is Undefined. Since these are different data types, if we compare them with strict equality, triple equals, we get false. But if we compare them with abstract equality, double equals, we get true. So JavaScript does consider these to be relatively equal, since they are both basically blank. So if you need to check to see if a value is either null or undefined, you can check for abstract equality by using the double equals sign and compare it to either null or undefined. Both will return the same result. This has been a 90-second JavaScript January.
